draft.title: Federation
card: On 1 January 1901 the six separate British colonies joined to form one nation, the Commonwealth of Australia. This joining is called Federation.
Before Federation, each colony had its own government and its own laws. Each also charged taxes on goods crossing its borders.
Many people wanted shared defence, so one national force could protect the whole continent rather than six separate colonies.
Many also wanted free trade between the colonies, with no taxes on goods crossing borders. Others wanted a national identity, a sense of being one people.
draft.remember: Federation joined six colonies into one nation for defence, free trade and a shared identity.

opts: Six colonies joined to form the Commonwealth of Australia
Australia became fully independent of the British Empire
The colonies were first settled by British officials
Six colonies became six separate and self-governing nations
a.why: On that date the six colonies joined as one nation, the Commonwealth of Australia. Becoming fully independent is tempting, but the card says only that the colonies joined together, and it does not say the new nation cut all ties with Britain.
a.clue: Think about what the word Federation means.

b.q: Before 1901, a wool trader in Albury sent bales to Melbourne and paid a tax at the border. Which reason for Federation does this show?
opts: Votes for people on the goldfields
b.why: Colonies taxed goods crossing their borders, so the trader paid a tax. Joining as one nation allowed free trade between the colonies. Defence and identity were also reasons, but they do not involve taxes on goods.
b.clue: Look for what the trader had to pay at the border.

a.best: Six colonies joined to form the Commonwealth of Australia
